candidates.name: PROSPECT (on Intuitive Machines IM-4)
candidates.why: The home of the OU-led ProSPA now that it no longer flies on Luna 27. Could replace or rename the Luna 27 entry.

fields.landed_coords: { lat: -84.5, lon: 31.5 } (current planned site, subject to NASA confirmation)
fields.description: ESA’s PROSPECT package will drill up to about 1 m into the regolith near the lunar south pole and analyse the samples for water and other volatiles. It flies on Intuitive Machines’ Nova-C lander under NASA’s CLPS programme (task CP-22).
fields.ou_involvement: The Open University leads development of ProSPA, the package’s analytical laboratory, which heats drilled samples in sealed ovens and measures the gases with mass spectrometers.

candidates.name: Chandrayaan-2
candidates.why: Listed on the CEI mission page and the OU space research page. Follows directly from the Chandrayaan-1 entry.

fields.description: India’s second lunar mission. Its orbiter has mapped the Moon since 2019. The Vikram lander was lost during landing.
fields.ou_involvement: The Centre for Electronic Imaging characterised the CCD236 swept-charge devices for the CLASS X-ray spectrometer, which maps the Moon’s elements. It analysed radiation damage, showed a factor-of-two gain in radiation hardness, and produced the instrument’s quantum-efficiency calibration. CLASS uses 16 CCD236s.

candidates.name: AlSat Nano
candidates.why: The credits already name “AlSat Nano mission, The Open University” (used for the UKube-1 image), but there is no entry. It carried the OU’s C3D2 camera.

fields.orbit: 680 km sun-synchronous, launched 26 Sep 2016 on PSLV-C35
fields.description: A joint UK–Algeria 3U CubeSat, built with Surrey Space Centre to train Algerian engineers and test UK payloads in orbit.
fields.ou_involvement: The OU built the C3D2 camera with XCAM and e2v, a follow-on to the C3D flown on UKube-1. It carried three e2v Sapphire CMOS sensors and took AlSat Nano’s first colour image on 3 December 2016.

candidates.name: ExoMars 2016 Schiaparelli
candidates.why: An OU scientist was on the lander’s surface payload team. Its carrier (TGO) is already in the file.

sources.t: Esposito et al. 2018: DREAMS, Space Sci Rev

fields.description: ESA’s entry, descent and landing demonstrator. It reached Mars with the Trace Gas Orbiter but crashed on 19 October 2016 after a software error in the final descent.
fields.ou_involvement: Manish Patel (OU) was a co-investigator on DREAMS, the lander’s environmental sensor package, which included the MicroARES electric-field sensor.

candidates.name: Mars Express
candidates.why: Carried Beagle 2. An OU scientist is a co-investigator on its orbiter instruments.

fields.description: ESA’s first Mars mission, in orbit since December 2003. Confirmed to the end of 2026, with an extension to 2028 to support JAXA’s MMX.
fields.ou_involvement: Mars Express carried the OU-led Beagle 2 lander. John Murray (OU) was a co-investigator on the orbiter’s instrument teams (HRSC camera), per ESA’s payload documentation.

candidates.name: WSO-UVS (Spektr-UF)

fields.description: A Russian-led ultraviolet space observatory for 115–310 nm, with Spain and Japan as partners.
fields.ou_involvement: The Centre for Electronic Imaging studies radiation damage to the CCD camera’s sensors and their ability to integrate for long periods at very low noise.

candidates.name: International Mars Ice Mapper (I-MIM)
candidates.why: The OU received £2 million, then £1.2 million, from UKSA for the imager detector. It is a significant OU instrument role.

fields.description: A proposed Canadian-led orbiter to map shallow water ice on Mars ahead of human exploration.
fields.ou_involvement: Manish Patel’s team is developing the imaging detector for a visible–infrared multispectral imager, with the University of Bern.
